title: Energy-Corrected SPT N-Value (N₆₀)

N₆₀.description: SPT N-value corrected to 60% energy ratio

N_field.description: Raw field blow count (last 300 mm of drive)

applicability: All modern correlations reference N₆₀. If using automatic hammer with ER = 85%, then N₆₀ = N_field × (85/60) = N_field × 1.42. Critical to know hammer energy ratio.

title: Fully Corrected SPT — (N₁)₆₀
equation: (N₁)₆₀ = N_field × CE × CB × CS × CR × CN

CB.description: Borehole diameter correction (1.0 for 65–115 mm; 1.05 for 150 mm; 1.15 for 200 mm)

CS.description: Sampler correction (1.0 with liner; 1.1–1.3 without liner when designed for one)

CR.description: Rod length correction (0.75 for 3–4 m; 0.85 for 4–6 m; 0.95 for 6–10 m; 1.0 for >10 m)

applicability: Required for liquefaction analysis and density-based correlations. For simple bearing capacity/settlement correlations, N₆₀ alone is often sufficient.

title: Overburden Correction Factor — Liao & Whitman

σ'v.description: Vertical effective stress at test depth

applicability: Most widely used form. Cap at 1.7 prevents over-correction at shallow depths. Kayen et al. (1992) form: CN = 2.2/(1.2 + σ'v/Pa). Boulanger & Idriss (2014): CN = (Pa/σ'v)^m where m varies with Dr.

title: Friction Angle from SPT — Hatanaka & Uchida
applicability: For clean sands. Based on high-quality frozen sand samples. Range: (N₁)₆₀ = 5 → φ' ≈ 30°; 20 → 40°; 40 → 48°. Upper bound for well-graded sands; lower bound for uniform fine sands.

title: Undrained Shear Strength from SPT (Clays)

f₁.description: Empirical factor (4–6 kPa per blow, varies with plasticity)

applicability: Very approximate. Stroud (1975): f₁ = 4.4 for PI ≈ 15; f₁ = 6.0 for PI ≈ 50. SPT is unreliable in soft clays (N < 5) — use vane shear or CPT instead. More reliable in stiff-hard clays where other tests are difficult.

title: Relative Density from SPT — Cubrinovski & Ishihara

Cd.description: Empirical coefficient (varies 35–55 depending on fines, gradation, mineralogy)

applicability: Cd ≈ 41 for clean sand (D₅₀ ≈ 0.2–2.0 mm). Cd higher for fine/silty sands, lower for coarse/gravelly sands. Approximate relationship — significant scatter. Example: (N₁)₆₀ = 25, Cd = 41 → Dr ≈ 78%.

title: Young's Modulus from SPT (Sands)

E.description: Drained Young's modulus (secant at working stress level)

α.description: Empirical multiplier (varies 0.5–1.5 MPa/blow depending on soil type and strain level)

applicability: Very approximate. Webb (1969): E ≈ 0.5(N₆₀+15) for sand. Bowles: E ≈ 7×√N₆₀ for OC sand. Denver & Skov (1988): E ≈ 40+N₆₀ for NC sand. Wide scatter — use CPT-based methods for better stiffness estimates.

title: SPT Energy Measurement (Force × Velocity Method)

E_delivered.description: Energy delivered to drill rod at measurement point

F(t).description: Force measured by load cell vs time

v(t).description: Velocity measured by accelerometer vs time

L.description: Length of drill rod from hammer to measurement point

c.description: Stress wave velocity in steel rod (~5120 m/s)

applicability: Integration over first 2L/c captures the direct blow energy before reflections. Energy ratio ER = E_delivered / (474 J) × 100%. Per ASTM D4633 (SPT Energy Measurement). Recommended practice: measure energy for every project to calibrate correlations.
